newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude prices ease, buying dries up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude prices ease, buying dries up.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices eased with broader markets Thursday, with only one report of local cargo movements, traders said.

Traders said all or part of a cargo of South Blend crude owned by Chevron was slated to be shipped to Hawaii refineries. The 400,000 barrels of oil, an ANS lookalike, would cost about $1.25 a barrel under September West Texas Intermediate (WTI), including transportation.
Traders said BHP's refinery in Hawaii could take part of the cargo.
Meanwhile, the spot price of Alaska North Slope crude remained at $1.97 a barrel under WTI.
The discount, which has shrunk since a mid-June cargo sold at minus $2.08, is expected to hold steady for the rest of the month.
Kern River and Wilmington grades were flat Thursday after rising with postings the day before.
